content.text: No exclusivity language binds Bluefly anywhere in the agreement. Section 14.16 is mutual and affirmatively preserves our freedom to contract elsewhere; § 14.11 is only a no-resale restriction (not an exclusive-purchase covenant), and the only "exclusive" usages relate to warranty disclaimers and license grants.

input.quote: Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others.
input.rationale: No exclusivity, sole-source, or requirements-purchase obligation binds Customer. Section 14.16 (Freedom of Action) is expressly mutual ("Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others"), which affirmatively preserves our right to procure hosting and related services from other suppliers, so there is no asymmetry to flag. A regex sweep for "sole supplier/sole source/sole provider/all of its requirements/shall not procure/shall not purchase/preferred provider/minimum volume/competing" returned no hits. The only uses of "exclusive" are unrelated to dealing restrictions: § 4.3 (charges exclusive of taxes), § 5.2 (exclusive warranties disclaimer), and § 5.4/§ 12.1 (nonexclusive license grants to Customer). Section 14.11 restricts only resale of the Services, which is a scope-of-use limit rather than an exclusive-purchase covenant, and § 13.1 in fact lets Customer terminate without termination charges if it disagrees with IBM changes. The preferred position (no exclusivity obligation on Customer) is met, so no redline is required.
